source.title: Mechanistic Interpretability as Statistical Estimation: A Variance Analysis of EAP-IG
source.authors: Maxime Méloux; François Portet; Maxime Peyrard

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates IOI circuit discovery and reports that circuit structure and faithfulness vary with resampling and methodological choices, refining claims about circuit stability and evaluation.
record.gate_note: The study does not test the original 26-head circuit's stated head roles, backup heads, or ablation of everything outside that circuit. It evaluates circuits found with EAP-family procedures and reports circuit error and structural overlap. Cited findings from other papers are not recorded as results. The detailed GPT-2 table with hyperparameter results has more listed configurations than clearly aligned result entries, so those ambiguously aligned values are omitted.
record.test_reason: Runs EAP-family circuit discovery on IOI in GPT-2 small and Llama-3.2-1B(-Instruct). It reports structural overlap and circuit error under resampling, prompt paraphrasing, estimator, aggregation and ablation choices, and noise amplitude. It argues the found circuit is conditioned on these methodological choices. It never compares against the original 26-head circuit.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors add three points. Bootstrap resampling is far less stable than distribution shift or paraphrasing. Llama models are less stable than GPT-2 small. Circuit-discovery methods recover a structure conditioned on methodological choices, not a unique population-level mechanism. They recommend bootstrap stability reporting, e.g. mean Jaccard above 0.8.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes EAP, EAP-IG variants, and circuit stability rather than reproducing the original IOI circuit's head-level patching and ablation tests.
record.method_sensitivity: For IOI, circuit overlap and error vary with estimator and configuration; the paper also reports different structural overlap and error under bootstrap, meta-dataset sampling, and prompt paraphrasing.

fits_no_version.finding: Exact per-input CMA edge scores for IOI in GPT-2 small have CV around 0.5, and EAP raises the CV above 1 (Fig. 7).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Per-edge causal importance for IOI varies strongly across inputs, and attribution patching amplifies this variance.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306 (2026)
record.problems: Exact CMA variance analysis is restricted to gpt2-small and selected tasks because of computational cost. Circuit discovery focuses on the EAP family; the paper notes that its stability metrics treat edges equally. Some detailed GPT-2 hyperparameter table entries are not clearly aligned with all listed configurations in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted the ambiguously aligned GPT-2 hyperparameter results in Table 9 and results for other models/tasks that do not test the specified GPT-2 IOI prompt-variant claim. Also omitted circuit-size and KL-divergence entries where they were not needed for the tested versions.

untested.parts: The 26 heads, 7 classes, head roles, and the original faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria are not examined.
No name-mover ablation or backup-head self-repair.
Llama circuits are found, but head classes and roles are not compared, and there is no component reuse across tasks.
Only EAP-family estimators are compared, and only among themselves. There is no comparison with ACDC or path patching, and no overlap with the original IOI circuit.
The original circuit's faithfulness and completeness under different ablations are not evaluated.
Name orders, specific templates and prompts with more names are not tested separately, and head roles are not checked.

missing.what: Noise-amplitude sweep for IOI in GPT-2 small: circuit error and pairwise Jaccard change with Gaussian counterfactual amplitude. The Jaccard CV peaks near amplitude 0.2, averaged across tasks.
GPT-2 small IOI hyperparameter sensitivity: Jaccard to median ranges 0.042–1.000 and circuit error 0.10–0.14. Row alignment is ambiguous (7 values for 8 configurations).
Llama-3.2-1B IOI configurations: Jaccard to median 0.016–1.000, circuit sizes 5–448, error 0.59–0.77.
Llama-3.2-1B and Instruct IOI under bootstrap, meta-dataset and paraphrase sampling.

record.verdict_notes: Circuits here are EAP-family edge subgraphs, never compared with the Wang et al. head circuit. Links to V4 and V5 are therefore indirect, about IOI circuit discovery in general. The R3 'support' label in the record was invalid because R3 is the median reference. In Llama, all IOI circuits fail to reproduce the model on 69–82% of inputs.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test the original 26 heads, seven head classes, their stated roles, or the original faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria.
Does not ablate main name-mover heads or test self-repair by backup heads.
Runs IOI circuit discovery on other models, but does not test whether the original head classes and roles carry IOI there, or whether components are reused for other tasks.
Compares EAP-family estimators and related configuration choices, not a broad range of independent circuit-finding methods or ablation types.
Tests resampling, prompt paraphrasing, estimator and hyperparameter choices; does not assess all possible evaluation metrics or prompt distributions.
Tests prompt paraphrasing for IOI, but not specifically name orders, templates, or prompts with more names, nor whether the original head roles persist.
